evidence: src/domain/Order.ts: class Order enforces the order invariants (constructor validation, advanceTo using nextByStatus, cancel) and throws DomainError
src/domain/Product.ts: class Product enforces the stock invariants (reserve/release via private assertValidQuantity) and throws DomainError
src/domain/OrderStatus.ts: orderStatuses tuple and OrderStatus type are the single status vocabulary, used by Order.ts and OrderRepository.ts
src/domain/OrderRepository.ts and src/domain/ProductRepository.ts: matching repository ports (findById/save/listByStatus or list) for the two entities
src/domain/DomainError.ts: the one error type all domain invariants use

Minor overlap: positive-integer quantity check appears in the Order constructor and in Product.assertValidQuantity; the status order appears in both orderStatuses and nextByStatus (the Record type keeps membership in sync)
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
src/domain is one coherent domain model for ordering and stock. It has two entities, `Order` and `Product`, each with its own repository port (`OrderRepository`, `ProductRepository`). They share one error type (`DomainError`) and one status vocabulary (`OrderStatus`). No file wanders into an unrelated concern such as transport, persistence or DTOs. Every file uses the module's own abstractions the same way: all invariant failures throw `DomainError`, the status type comes from `OrderStatus.ts`, and both repositories follow the same shape (`findById`/`save`/list).

Two small overlaps exist, and I don't think either rises to a rubric failure:
1. The "positive integer quantity" check is written twice. It appears in the `Order` constructor's line check and again in `Product.assertValidQuantity`. Each sits inside the entity that owns that data, which is normal for an entity-based model. A shared Quantity value object would be cleaner, but leaving it out isn't a real boundary problem.
2. The status order appears twice. It is set by the `orderStatuses` tuple and again by the `nextByStatus` map in `Order.advanceTo`. The `Record<OrderStatus, ...>` type means adding a new status forces a compile error until the map is updated, so the two can't silently drift on membership. The lifecycle rule itself (moves and cancellation) lives only in `Order`.

Each rule otherwise lives in one place, so the module passes.
